main_body: A flat stone-brick wall/paving texture patch (4x3 tiles) of running-bond bricks with dark mortar joints, seen face-on as a tiling terrain surface.
top_band: none as a standing object; the scan only shows repeating brick courses (light highlight row L=176, mid face L=143, then darker mortar rows L=115 and 90), not a top surface
evidence: This is a seamless terrain tile pattern (brick wall face or paving) and not a standing object, so the 3/4 top-plus-front contract does not apply. The column scan shows a repeating brick course: 1 row highlight, about 5 rows face, 2 rows mortar shadow. There is no standing volume to fail. Kind 'terrain' matches.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 5 distinct colours and a median of 5 per tile, against 26 per tile and 80 colours for the grass reference and 7 and 7 for the paving reference. It is close to the paving reference on those counts but far below the grass. The mortar and dark edge pixels are 100% neutral, so the outline is a neutral grey-black line rather than a tinted dark material tone. Each brick is a flat tan face with a highlight row on top, a dark right and bottom edge and a few scattered speckle dots, which is shallow. The paving reference has stone-by-stone shading and more varied cobble texture, so the candidate reads flatter and more sticker-like. Flat-fill coverage is 0% only because of the speckle dots. Overall it is thinner than the references.
